unitChecks.reason: EN covers hunting on western border, crossing river, cinnabar-robed elder on white horse, and quoted warning to return.
EN covers concealing the warning, crossing, and days of great catch.
EN drops 馳射之 and turns 說所見 into omen; Chinese is gallop-and-shoot then narrate what was seen. Literal covers seeing the hare, galloping to shoot, horse fall injury, and narrating what was seen.
Current EN misses litter return to palace and 引俊屬以後事 entrusting posthumous affairs. Current literal obscures 引俊 as summoning and who entrusts 以後事.
EN adds western year 348 CE not present in 永和四年; source states Yonghe 4, fifteen years, age fifty-two. Literal covers death in Yonghe 4, fifteen years on throne, age fifty-two sui.
Current EN reads 僭號 as ordinary succession; Chinese is illegitimate assumption of imperial title. Literal already marks 僭號 as illegitimately assuming imperial title and 追諡文明皇帝.
EN adds parenthetical defector general absent from bare name heading 慕容翰. Literal correctly gives only the name Murong Han.
EN covers courtesy name Yuanyong and eldest concubine-born son of Hui.
EN omits 猿臂 and weakens 多權略 to cunning; source stresses ape-arms archery and abundant stratagem. Literal covers 雄豪、權略、猿臂工射、膂力過人.
EN covers Hui marveling and entrusting hard front-line fighting charge.
EN covers campaign success and far-near fear of his reputation.
EN covers garrisoning Liaodong so Goguryeo dared not raid.
EN covers kindness, love of learning, and willing followership from gentry to ranks.
EN reduces 敬愛 to honored and labels 奔 as defection without deep respect-and-love. Literal covers fleeing to Liao and being deeply respected and loved.
EN collapses Han’s fear of harming Yan, deceitful counsel, and Lan’s halt into one vague paraphrase. Literal covers 乘勝深入、慮成本國之害、詭說、蘭遂不進.
EN covers Shi Hu’s campaign, Huang’s personal raid north of Lingzhi, Liao’s pursuit debate, and Han’s quoted caution.
EN omits 燕王自來; Chinese stresses the King of Yan came in person with elite troops. Literal covers personal coming and picked sharp soldiers and horses.
EN drops 兵者凶器 and compresses 戰有危慮; closing south-defence question remains. Literal covers weapons as ill-omened tools, battle peril, and 何以南禦.
EN covers Lan’s anger at prior deceitful counsel and refusal to enter Han’s plans again.
EN omits 率眾 and 果; Chinese has Lan lead the host and indeed suffer great defeat. Literal covers leading the host to pursue and 蘭果大敗.
EN invents secretly for Yan’s good and drops 皆此類也 summarizing pattern of loyalty amid events. Literal covers dwelling in enemy state, establishing loyalty through affairs, and 皆此類也.
EN covers Liao’s flight and Han’s northern resort to Yuwen Gui.
EN omits 既而逃; Chinese first has Han flee, then Gui send over a hundred picked cavalry. Literal covers flight then Gui sending 勁騎百餘.
EN covers calling to pursuers that he longs to return and will not turn back.
EN omits 自取死也 warning that pressing him brings their own death. Literal misreads 相逼 as force each other rather than do not press me.
EN covers long sojourn among them and regret at not having killed them.
EN anticipates 刀鐶 with ring it; this unit only has 射中 before the ring appears next. Literal covers hundred-pace set blade and if shot hits then withdraw.
EN covers the miss branch inviting them to come forward.
EN covers setting the blade, first-shot hit on the ring, and pursuers scattering.
EN covers arrival and Huang’s rich favor and ceremony.
EN covers Jianyuan 2 campaign, stray arrow wound, and long illness.
EN omits 疾漸愈 and home self-test riding before the report of private practice. Literal covers gradual recovery, home riding test, report of private practice, suspicion of the unusual.
EN turns 賜死 into sent poison and 忌 into feared; poison appears only later in 仰藥. Literal’s plain envied is awkward for 素忌; needs long jealousy/wariness then granted death.
EN understates 罪不容誅 and softens return to face authorities; needs full dying speech sense. Literal mishandles 歸罪有司 as returning guilt to officials rather than submitting to them.
EN covers sparing public marketplace display and death as life/mercy.
EN covers rebel Hu occupying the Divine Land, unmet vow to swallow caitiffs, late king’s aim, mountain-sea duty.
EN covers failed aim, dying regret, and fate.
EN covers drinking the poison and dying.
EN correctly renders the section name Yang Yu.
EN covers courtesy name Shilun and Wuzhong in Right Beiping.
EN covers early orphanhood, dead brothers, clan neglect, uncle Dan’s marvel and quoted praise.
EN covers He Yan summoning him as chief clerk.
EN reduces 忌而不能任 to distrusted and drops refusal/inability to employ. Literal covers transfer to 治中從事 and jealous inability to employ.
EN covers Shi Le taking Ji and asking who among Youzhou gentlemen is most worthy.
EN covers Song naming Liu Han of Yan as a plain virtuous elder.
EN covers Yang Yu of Beiping as talent for handling affairs.
EN singular him after two nominees; Le asks why Duke Wang did not employ them. Literal correctly uses them for 何以不任 after two names.
EN covers failure to employ them as why Wang was captured by Le.
EN covers Le about to employ him and Yu fleeing in disguise.
EN covers Duan Juan’s Jin titles and humble invitation of Yu.
EN covers Confucius/Bi Xi gourd and Yi Yin’s lord-people sayings in Yu’s speech to Cheng Pan.
EN covers Juan’s summons as not in vain.
EN misreads 軌跡所及易水而已 as no refuge beyond Yi; source means order’s reach ends at Yi. Literal covers Huaxia split, nine provinces torn, tracks only to Yi River.
EN covers reclusive waiting for peace as waiting for Yellow River to clear. Literal redundantly doubles waiting for the river to clear and muddies 偃蹇考槃.
EN covers the brief life-span question.
EN covers ancients’ white-colt sigh over fleeting time.
EN covers Shaoyou’s saying that commandery clerk shades posterity, still more a state chancellor.
EN covers tracing Yi Yin and Confucius and knowing the timely spring.
EN covers Yu accepting the summons.
EN covers Palace Director, Central Army General, and upper-minister rank.
EN covers serving five Duan lords with deep respect.
EN covers remonstrance opening with cherish-benevolence befriend-neighbors as state treasure.
EN covers generational marriage ties, Huang as virtuous lord, and warning against war harming the people.
EN covers fear that disaster will arise from this.
EN turns 兩追前失 into forget quarrels; Chinese asks both to remedy former faults and renew good faith. Literal covers remedy former faults, 通款如初, Taishan security, and resting-shoulder benefit.
EN covers Liao’s refusal to follow the counsel.
EN covers outgoing appointment as Yan commandery grand warden.
EN covers Lingzhi’s fall, surrender of the commandery, Beiping post, and summons as Left Assistant.
EN covers concurrent marshal post under Ma Qiu while Left Assistant when Liao sought reception.
EN covers Qiu’s defeat, Yu seized, about to be taken to Huang.
EN softens 素聞名 to admired and vague senior major; Chinese appoints 郎中令 then 大將軍左司馬. Literal’s plain had heard is awkward for 素聞; needs long-heard name and exact offices.
EN covers pre-planning east Goguryeo and north Yuwen victories and Huang’s heavy reliance.
EN covers Helong capital move and Yu’s plans shaping walls and palace works Huang built.
EN drops near daily service, ranked virtues 謙恭清儉剛簡慈篤, and court-apex yet plain-cloth likeness. Literal covers rising favor, full character list, 朝端, and 布衣之士.
EN covers burying cut-off exiles, aiding orphans, treating all gentry, winning esteem.
EN thins Lu Chen’s quote: drops Jin clear peace lived through, full virtue string, and 陽士倫. Literal covers 晉之清平、忠清簡毅篤信義烈 and 如陽士倫者實亦未幾.
EN covers death at sixty-two and Huang’s deep mourning.

knownDecisions.before: They carried him home; he briefed Murong Jun on the succession.
knownDecisions.after: He was carried back to the palace in a litter and summoned Jun to entrust him with affairs after his death.
knownDecisions.sourceQuote: 輦而還宮，引俊屬以後事。
knownDecisions.sourceReason: 引俊屬以後事 describes summoning Jun and entrusting him with subsequent affairs, not merely briefing him on succession; 宮 is the palace, and 輦 specifies litter conveyance.

knownDecisions.before: Carried on litter returned palace, led Jun to entrust later affairs.
knownDecisions.after: He returned to the palace in a litter and summoned Jun, entrusting him with affairs after his death.
knownDecisions.sourceQuote: 輦而還宮，引俊屬以後事。
knownDecisions.sourceReason: 引俊 here summons Jun; 屬以後事 entrusts him with the affairs to follow the dying ruler, as the next sentence confirms. Led Jun to entrust later affairs obscures who entrusts whom.

knownDecisions.before: After Murong Jun took the throne he posthumously styled his father Emperor Wenming.
knownDecisions.after: When Murong Jun assumed the imperial title in usurpation, he posthumously honored his father as Emperor Wenming.
knownDecisions.sourceReason: 俊僭號 means Jun’s assumption of an imperial title, not his earlier succession to the throne. Preserve 僭 and avoid conflating the later imperial claim with succession after Huang’s death. The literal field already distinguishes this action.

additionalCorrections.before: Later he charged a white hare, was thrown and hurt, and told the omen.
additionalCorrections.after: Later he saw a white hare, galloped to shoot it; his horse fell and he was injured, then he told what he had seen.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 後見白兔，馳射之，馬倒被傷，乃說所見。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 後見白兔馳射之 is see then gallop-and-shoot, not merely charge; 乃說所見 narrates what was seen, not an omen gloss.

additionalCorrections.before: He died in Yonghe 4 (348 CE) after fifteen years on the throne, aged fifty-two.
additionalCorrections.after: He died in the fourth year of Yonghe after fifteen years on the throne, aged fifty-two.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 以永和四年死，在位十五年，時年五十二。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Chinese gives only 永和四年 with tenure and age; the western year 348 CE is not in the source sentence.

additionalCorrections.before: Murong Han (defector general).
additionalCorrections.after: Murong Han.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 慕容翰
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Unit is the bare personal-name heading 慕容翰; parenthetical defector general is editorial addition.

additionalCorrections.before: He was bold, cunning, a superb archer, and immensely strong.
additionalCorrections.after: He was heroic and bold, full of stratagems, ape-armed and skilled at archery, with strength that surpassed others.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 性雄豪，多權略，猿臂工射，膂力過人。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 性雄豪多權略 needs heroic boldness and abundant stratagem, not cunning; 猿臂工射 must keep the ape-arms detail.

additionalCorrections.before: Duan Liao honored him after his defection.
additionalCorrections.after: When he fled to Duan Liao, he was deeply respected and loved by Liao.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 及奔段遼，深為遼所敬愛。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 及奔段遼 states flight to Liao; 深為遼所敬愛 is deep respect and love, not merely honored after defection.

additionalCorrections.before: After the defeat at Liucheng, Duan Lan wanted to push on, but Murong Han feigned advice that spared Yan a deeper strike.
additionalCorrections.after: After the defeat at Liucheng, Duan Lan wanted to ride the victory and push deep; Murong Han, fearing this would bring harm on his native state, gave Lan deceitful counsel, and Lan then did not advance.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 柳城之敗，段蘭欲乘勝深入，翰慮成本國之害，詭說于蘭，蘭遂不進。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Must keep 乘勝深入, 慮成本國之害, 詭說于蘭, and 蘭遂不進 as distinct propositions.

additionalCorrections.before: Murong Huang’s host is elite.
additionalCorrections.after: The King of Yan has come in person; his soldiers and horses are elite.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 燕王自來，士馬精銳。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 燕王自來 is personal arrival of the Yan king; 士馬精銳 is elite troops and mounts, not host alone.

additionalCorrections.before: War is peril—if you lose here, how will you hold the south?”
additionalCorrections.after: Weapons are ill-omened tools, and battle holds peril; if you lose here, how will you defend the south?”
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 兵者凶器，戰有危慮，若其失利，何以南禦乎！」
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 兵者凶器 is the opening idiom and must be kept; 戰有危慮 and 何以南禦 close the warning.

additionalCorrections.before: He chased Huang and was crushed.
additionalCorrections.after: He then led his forces to pursue Huang, and Lan was indeed crushingly defeated.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 乃率眾追皝，蘭果大敗。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 乃率眾追皝 states leading the host in pursuit; 蘭果大敗 marks the indeed-fulfilled great defeat.

additionalCorrections.before: Even in exile Murong Han worked secretly for Yan’s good.
additionalCorrections.after: Although Murong Han dwelt in an enemy state, he established loyalty through the course of events—all cases were of this kind.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 翰雖處仇國，因事立忠，皆此類也。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 因事立忠 is loyalty shown amid events, not secret work for Yan; 皆此類也 must remain as the summary.

additionalCorrections.before: Yuwen Gui sent a hundred picked riders after him.
additionalCorrections.after: Han then fled, and Gui sent over a hundred picked cavalry to pursue him.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 既而逃，歸乃遣勁騎百餘追之。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 既而逃 is Han’s flight before 歸乃遣勁騎百餘追之; both steps are required.

additionalCorrections.before: You know my archery—do not force a fight.
additionalCorrections.after: You know my bow and arrows well enough—do not press me and bring death on yourselves.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 吾之弓矢，汝曹足知，無為相逼，自取死也。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 無為相逼自取死也 warns against pressing him and thereby seeking their own deaths; archery fame alone is incomplete.

additionalCorrections.before: My bow and arrows, you lot fully know; do not force each other, self-seeking death.
additionalCorrections.after: My bow and arrows you lot fully know; do not press me and seek your own deaths.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 吾之弓矢，汝曹足知，無為相逼，自取死也。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 相逼 is pressing the speaker, not forcing each other; 自取死也 is bringing death on yourselves.

additionalCorrections.before: Plant a blade at a hundred paces—if I ring it, withdraw;
additionalCorrections.after: Plant a blade at a hundred paces—if I hit it, withdraw;
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 汝可百步豎刀，吾射中者，汝便宜反；
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 吾射中者 means if the shot hits; 刀鐶 appears only in the next unit and should not be imported here.

additionalCorrections.before: When he tried riding at home, informers called it sedition.
additionalCorrections.after: Later, as his illness gradually improved, he tried riding at home to test himself; someone reported that Han was privately practising riding and suspected something extraordinary.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 後疾漸愈，於其家中騎馬自試，或有人告翰私習騎，疑為非常。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 後疾漸愈 and 騎馬自試 precede the denunciation; 私習騎 and 疑為非常 are report and suspicion, not a bare sedition gloss.

additionalCorrections.before: Huang, who had always feared him, sent him poison.
additionalCorrections.after: Huang, who had long been jealous of him, thereupon granted him death.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 皝素忌之，遂賜死焉。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 素忌之 is long jealousy or wariness; 賜死 is granting death, while poison is only stated later in 仰藥而死.

additionalCorrections.before: Huang plain envied him; thereupon granted death.
additionalCorrections.after: Huang had long been jealous of him; thereupon granted him death.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 皝素忌之，遂賜死焉。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 素忌之 needs long-standing jealousy or wariness; plain envied is unclear wording for the same fact.

additionalCorrections.before: Murong Han told the messenger, “I fled in fear and deserved death, yet I would not die in a foreign hall, so I came home to face judgment.
additionalCorrections.after: Nearing death Murong Han told the envoy, “Han harbored distrust and fled abroad; my crime is too great for death to atone; I could not leave my bones in a rebel court, so I returned to submit to the authorities.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 翰臨死謂使者曰：「翰懷疑外奔，罪不容誅，不能以骸骨委賊庭，故歸罪有司。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 罪不容誅 marks guilt beyond mere execution; 歸罪有司 is submitting to officials, after refusing 賊庭 bones.

additionalCorrections.before: Han nearing death told the envoy: “Han harbored suspicion and fled abroad; crime does not permit execution; could not cast bones in the bandit court; therefore returned guilt to the responsible officials.
additionalCorrections.after: Han nearing death told the envoy: “Han harbored suspicion and fled abroad; the crime is too great for death to atone; I could not cast my bones in the bandit court; therefore I returned to submit to the responsible officials.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 翰臨死謂使者曰：「翰懷疑外奔，罪不容誅，不能以骸骨委賊庭，故歸罪有司。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 歸罪有司 means submitting oneself to the authorities for punishment, not returning guilt onto them.

additionalCorrections.before: Under Wang Jun he rose to administration aide but was distrusted.
additionalCorrections.after: When Wang Jun held the province, Yu was transferred to administration aide; Jun was jealous and would not employ him.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 王浚領州，轉治中從事，忌而不能任。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 轉治中從事 is the transfer; 忌而不能任 is jealousy plus refusal or failure to employ, not distrust alone.

additionalCorrections.before: Shi Le asked, "If what you say is so, why did Duke Wang not employ him?"
additionalCorrections.after: Shi Le asked, "If what you say is so, why did Duke Wang not employ them?"
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 勒曰：「若如君言，王公何以不任？」
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Song has just named Liu Han and Yang Yu; 何以不任 refers to not employing them, not only him.

additionalCorrections.before: Cheng Pan replied, “China is shattered; beyond the Yi River there is no refuge.
additionalCorrections.after: Cheng Pan replied, “Now Huaxia is split and crumbling, the nine provinces torn apart; where proper tracks reach is only as far as the Yi River.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 泮曰：「今華夏分崩，九州幅裂，軌跡所及，易水而已。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 軌跡所及易水而已 means civil order’s reach ends at the Yi, not that there is no refuge beyond it.

additionalCorrections.before: Desiring to recline and await the great penetration—waiting for the Yellow River to clear—is waiting for the river to clear.
additionalCorrections.after: To wish to live in proud reclusion (as in the “Kao pan”) and wait for a great opening is to wait for the Yellow River to run clear.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 欲偃蹇考槃，以待大通者，俟河之清也。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 偃蹇考槃以待大通 is reclusive waiting for a great thaw; 俟河之清也 is the single impossibility simile, not a doubled clause.

additionalCorrections.before: Let both sides forget old quarrels and restore peace so the realm stands firm as Taishan and the people can lay down their burdens.”
additionalCorrections.after: Let both sides remedy their former faults and renew good faith as at the beginning, so the state may have the security of Mount Tai and the common people receive the blessing of laying down their burdens.”
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 願兩追前失，通款如初，使國家有太山之安，蒼生蒙息肩之惠。」
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 兩追前失 is remedy former faults, not forget quarrels; 通款如初 and 太山/息肩 images must stay.

additionalCorrections.before: Murong Huang, who had long admired him, freed him at once, named him palace director, then promoted him to senior major on his staff.
additionalCorrections.after: Murong Huang, who had long heard of Yu’s name, at once ordered his bonds released, appointed him Palace Director, then promoted him to Grand General’s Left Major.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 皝素聞裕名，即命釋其囚，拜郎中令，遷大將軍左司馬。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 素聞裕名 is long hearing of the name; offices are 郎中令 then 大將軍左司馬, not a vague senior major.

additionalCorrections.before: Huang plain had heard Yu’s name; immediately ordered release his bonds; appointed Palace Director; promoted Grand General’s Left Major.
additionalCorrections.after: Huang had long heard of Yu’s name; immediately ordered his bonds released; appointed Palace Director; promoted him to Grand General’s Left Major.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 皝素聞裕名，即命釋其囚，拜郎中令，遷大將軍左司馬。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 素聞 needs had long heard; plain had heard is unclear, while the two office steps remain exact.

additionalCorrections.before: Though he rose above older favorites, he lived modestly and treated everyone like a poor scholar.
additionalCorrections.after: Although Yang Yu served Huang and grew daily closer, with favor and rank above the old retainers, his nature was humble, respectful, pure and frugal, firm, simple, kind and earnest; though he repeatedly held posts at the apex of the court, he was like a scholar in plain cloth.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 裕雖仕皝日近，寵秩在舊人之右，性謙恭清儉，剛簡慈篤，雖曆居朝端，若布衣之士。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Must keep 仕皝日近、寵秩在舊人之右, the virtue string 謙恭清儉剛簡慈篤, and 朝端若布衣之士.

additionalCorrections.before: Lu Chen of Fanyang once said, “In times of peace I have known many officials, but few match Yang Yu in loyalty, austerity, and steadfast faith.”
additionalCorrections.after: Earlier, Lu Chen of Fanyang always praised him, saying, “I have lived through Jin’s clear peace and have broadly observed many court gentlemen; loyal, pure, concise and resolute, steadfast in faith and fierce in righteousness—men like Yang Shilun are in truth few.”
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 初，范陽盧諶每稱之曰：「吾及晉之清平，曆觀朝士多矣，忠清簡毅，篤信義烈，如陽士倫者，實亦未幾。」
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: Quote needs 晉之清平, the full 忠清簡毅篤信義烈 string, and courtesy name 陽士倫, not a thinned paraphrase.

recordCorrections.sourceQuote: 曆事段氏五主，甚見尊重。
recordCorrections.sourceReason: 曆事段氏 means successively served the Duan house’s lords, not holding a post titled minister of the Duan.
